body:
It does listen to mouseup events on the window.

https://github.com/mbostock/d3/blob/master/src/behavior/drag.js#L19-L21

You can verify the correct behavior here:

http://bl.ocks.org/enjalot/raw/1378144

The problem is that this technique doesn't work with iframes, so in the iframed case you link, D3 has no way of capturing mouseup outside of the iframe.

But what I'm saying is that the window.mouseup solution _does_ work with iframes, at least outside of d3.

I re-made my jsFiddle example as a blocks, to make it identical to the d3 example I posted above:

http://bl.ocks.org/sfentress/5052881

In this example, you can drag the blue box outside of the iframe, and when you let go with you mouse the drag will be stopped.

In the d3 example, letting go with your mouse causes the elements to stick to the mouse when you return.

It appears that the preventDefault on mousedown prevents the mouseup from triggering if it occurs outside the iframe. However, without the preventDefault, text will be selected while dragging.

http://bl.ocks.org/mbostock/109620145f090cda1a7d

Here's an example that shows how to drag around a round div with text in it, while handling mouseup on the window and not selecting the text

http://bl.ocks.org/stepheneb/5054308

@stepheneb That approach would clobber a global "selectstart" event listener, but equivalently you could use a capturing selectstart listener and then use d3.event.preventDefault. But the real problem with that approach is that the "selectstart" event isn't supported on Firefox (or apparently standardized) and I'm not sure there's an equivalent.

Related, though, perhaps it would be better to set the CSS user-select property on draggable elements to "none". This appears to be supported by most browsers despite being not being standardized.

  http://bl.ocks.org/mbostock/878470b62de6c94d05bf

I think you'd still probably want to stopPropagation though, since conceptually the drag behavior has consumed the mousedown event.

@mbostock 

I wanted to let you know I am working on this issue in this topic branch: bubble-default-on-mousedown

https://github.com/concord-consortium/d3/compare/master...bubble-default-on-mousedown

I't's just the minimal (hacky) set of changes to get dragging using D3 in an iframed page working well enough for our purposes.

[I didn't commit the generated files since I thought that would obscure the actual changes that matter].

I also changed to listening to the document for the dragmove events. Without this I could drag objects past an iframe boundary (of course the object was clipped but I could get the object to disappear.

I also found that FF didn't generate a mouseup.drag when I dragged very quickly out of the iframe -- so I added a listener for mouseup

I tested this with both a draggable SVG circle and separately a draggable DIV.

Dragging the SVG circle works fine -- here's my test page -- it's using the release v3 of D3 so it still has the problem): http://bl.ocks.org/stepheneb/5059484

I created a separate test page for dragging a DIV aroun: http://bl.ocks.org/stepheneb/5059513

There is a problem with with dragging the DIV however, origin() just returns the string "div" not the coordinates.

I worked around the error with this change:
https://github.com/concord-consortium/d3/commit/13e7c0e0faca56f7ec3249f6a003aef1f5714486#L0R25

But because I am not generating a correct origin I can drag the DV out of bounds.

Combing my hacks in the D3 topic branch along with the next two steps in my main codebase now seems to have dragging working properly in Firefox, Sarai, Chrome, IE9, and IE10.
1. Disable display of user-selections (I used the Bourbon mixin: http://bourbon.io/docs/#user-select)
2. Had to add this for FF (???):
   
   document.ondragstart = function() { return false; };

The second of two closely-space clicks generates a dragstart event in FF which causes atom dragging to not work until after a subsequent click in the model not on an atom.

I'm not sure why this needs to be a dragstart listener on the document and not for example just on the atoms or SVG group container they are a part of.

FYI: the combined result (our code and the D3 topic branch) is visible on this page (select "Pull apart two polar molecules: in the select  list under the model and then drag the green start):

http://lab-staging.concord.org/examples/interactives/interactives.html#interactives/sam/intermolecular-attractions/2-comparing-dipole-dipole-to-london-dispersion.json

Now drags can be extended past the iframe boundary without losing the mouseup event and having the drag state stuck on.

issue.title: d3.behavior.zoom prevents expected focus behavior

repository.name: d3
repository.description: Bring data to life with SVG, Canvas and HTML. :bar_chart::chart_with_upwards_trend::tada:

issue.body:
d3.behavior.zoom cancels the mousedown event. This prevents the normal focus behavior. Specifically, focused inputs are no longer blurred as expected when clicking on the element with zoom behavior.

Example: http://bl.ocks.org/jfirebaugh/607420f372d98584ba31

issue.title: Use user-select: none instead of preventDefault for drag/zoom.

issue.body:
We also suppress the selectstart event, as IE9 doesn't support user-select.

Fixes #1288, #1099.

Note: untested in IE9.  Only tested in Chrome so far.

issue.body:
Work-in-progress. Supersedes #1322. Should fix #1321 #1288 #1099.

Tasks:
- [ ] Applying the drag behavior, zoom behavior or brush should set the tabindex attribute and outline style on the nearest HTML ancestor element (the ownerSVGElement when used within SVG, and the current element when used within HTML).
- [ ] If the tabindex attribute is already set, it should be preserved? What about the outline style? It might be safe to ignore this possibility.
- [x] The mousedown event should be cancelled (using preventDefault and stopPropagation).
- [x] The touchstart event should _not_ be cancelled for the drag behavior, as this disables draggable links. (Canceling mousedown does not prevent click, but canceling touchstart effectively does.)

body:
I'm still trying to get this to work in IE10.

Here's a very simple example of a draggable circle.

http://bl.ocks.org/stepheneb/5912718

The green circle is draggable.

The drag operation should be canceled when the drag extends outside of the iframe boundary and the drag is released.

This works in Chrome, Firefox, and Safari.

In IE10 (and probably IE9) a mouse-up (drag-end) event occurring outside the iframe is not processed correctly and the drag is now stuck on.

If you edit [src/event/drag.js](https://github.com/mbostock/d3/blob/master/src/event/drag.js) so that the selectstart and dragstart behaviors are not suppressed, does it work for you on IE10? Because that’s the only difference I can tell between the version you described earlier as working in all browsers.

With these changes I still see the same issue in IE10:

https://gist.github.com/stepheneb/5912718#file-d3-v3-modified-js-L1017-L1039
